name: Nullframe Arcpoint Wrist Interface
description:
A slim, matte-titanium wrist device worn on the dominant forearm, roughly 4cm wide. The face is a curved electroluminescent display showing a persistent analog clock overlay above a scrolling data feed — both readable simultaneously. BCI-sync port sits flush on the inner wrist edge, sealed with a magnetic dust cap.

The band is segmented carbon-composite with micro-hinge joints, adapting to chrome prosthetic wrists or standard flesh. A faint amber glow pulses at the port when syncing. Favored by analysts and junior specialists who want tactile confirmation of their neural feed without full ocular overlay.
functionality: BCI sync port for neural data confirmation, analog-digital dual display, notification haptics, encrypted short-burst comms, biometric lock keyed to wearer's pulse signature. Band adjusts for chrome wrist prosthetics via micro-hinge expansion.
what_it_says: Technically capable and deliberately understated — this person trusts hardware they can see over software they can only feel.
story_hooks: A firmware update pushed corp-side last quarter added passive environmental logging — most users don't know they're being recorded.
The BCI sync port accepts third-party chips with a known exploit; street hackers sell pre-loaded chips that mirror the device's output to a remote address.
A Tier 4 specialist was found with their Arcpoint smashed at the sync port — whatever data it last received has been flagged classified.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, minimalist wrist-mounted interface that reads as understated corporate tech. Sits flush against the forearm with a subtle presence despite its function—neither bulky nor delicate. The curved face catches light with a soft sheen, suggesting precision engineering.
physical_description.fit: Segmented and adjustable; conforms to standard human wrists and chrome prosthetic limbs alike. Sits snug against the skin or prosthetic surface without restriction, micro-hinge joints allow natural arm flexion.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte-titanium casing with carbon-composite segmented band. Electroluminescent display window with sealed BCI-sync port
physical_description.texture: Brushed titanium surface—smooth but non-reflective, reducing glare. Carbon-composite band has subtle ribbed segmentation beneath the fingers. Port cap has a smooth magnetic friction feel.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte gunmetal gray-silver with a faint amber electroluminescent glow at the sync port during operation. Display face is dark with soft green/white data feed text and analog clock markings.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic dust cap on BCI-sync port; segmented band self-adjusts via micro-hinge micro-locking system—no traditional clasp needed
distinctive_features: Dual persistent display: analog clock overlay + real-time data scrolling feed
Flush-mounted BCI-sync port with amber pulse indicator during neural sync
Ambidextrous design for dominant forearm wear
Chrome prosthetic compatibility—hinged segments conform to rigid synthetic wrists
Magnetic dust cap prevents environmental contamination of neural interface
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 luxury; specialized professional equipment. Not street-accessible. Suggests corporate affiliation or high-end independent contractor status.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by data analysts, neural-synced specialists, junior corp researchers, and augmented professionals who need tactile biofeedback without full ocular HUD. Signals competence and neural augmentation without ostentatious display.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to lightly worn. Kept clean and maintained; any visible wear would suggest field use (minor scratches on titanium, slight discoloration of dust cap from frequent port access).
